c.tagline: Where the Sava meets the Danube, and the party never quite stops.

taxi.fareNote: Use licensed companies (Pink Taxi, Beotaxi, Lux Taxi, Naxis) with visible taxi ID and working meter; airport transfers are often sold as a fixed price instead.

emergency.note: General EU-style emergency line 112 also works nationwide; fire brigade is 193.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Generally safe; usual pickpocket caution in the centre; football-match days can bring hooligan clashes

hood_desc: The historic old town packed with Kalemegdan Fortress, Knez Mihailova pedestrian street, and Skadarlija's bohemian taverns; best for first-time visitors who want everything walkable.
An upscale, leafy residential district anchored by the massive Church of Saint Sava, filled with cafes and boutiques; suits travelers wanting a quieter, local feel close to downtown.
A trendy riverside grid of low-rise buildings, specialty coffee shops, and Danube-side splav (raft club) nightlife; popular with younger travelers and digital nomads.
A fast-redeveloping riverside zone mixing gritty art squats with glossy new towers, malls, and the Sava promenade; good for travelers chasing nightlife and modern comforts.
A calmer former Habsburg-era fishing town on the Danube with cobbled lanes and the Gardoš Tower; ideal for travelers wanting a relaxed, authentic base away from downtown crowds.

water.note: Treated and generally safe, though a noticeable chlorine taste leads many visitors to prefer bottled water.

transit.pay: Buy a rechargeable contactless BusPlus card at kiosks/GSP outlets for the cheapest fares across bus, tram and trolleybus, or pay onboard with a single-ride SMS/driver ticket at a higher price. Many vehicles now also accept contactless bank-card tap-to-pay directly.
transit.hours: Most routes operate roughly 4:30/5:00 AM to 11:30 PM-midnight; a limited network of night lines (prefixed 'N') covers weekends into the early morning.
transit.note: Belgrade has no metro yet (a system is planned/under study); the BG Voz suburban rail supplements the bus/tram network on a few corridors.

bus: BAS Belgrade central bus station (intercity and international coaches)
ferry: Seasonal Sava/Danube river cruise and excursion boats

transit.m: A1 minibus shuttle to Slavija/city center (~40 min)
GSP city bus line 72 to Zeleni Venac (~45-50 min)

tip.r: Rounding up or leaving ~10% at restaurants is appreciated but not obligatory; for taxis, rounding to the nearest note is common.
